tasks.description: gap G-BATTLE-01: lib/forge/battle.ts (multi-candidate Design Battle) is fully implemented but unreachable from the production entrypoint — decide deliberately whether it becomes the production default
tasks.assignedWorker: claude to investigate; this is a product/architecture DECISION the mandate authorizes me to make, not one requiring human sign-off, but it is high-blast-radius (changes what a run actually produces) so it gets its own careful pass rather than a rushed tail-end change
tasks.outputs: DECISION (2026-08-25): Design Battle stays deliberately opt-in scaffolding, not the production default, for three concrete reasons found by reading both code paths side by side (lib/forge/orchestrator.ts's runExperienceForge vs lib/forge/battle.ts's runExperienceBattle), not a generic caution: (1) runExperienceForge has a real autonomous repair loop (repairCode, up to maxIterations) after the first critique; runExperienceBattle builds each candidate in exactly one pass with no repair step at all -- wiring it in today would mean every battle-selected site skips repair entirely, a quality regression dressed as a feature, not an improvement. (2) Cost multiplies by candidateCount (default 2) with zero integration into lib/capability/budget.ts's resolveBudgetTier -- the existing per-job budget ceiling (job.budgetCents) would not see or bound battle spend. (3) JobState's designDirections/distinctnessScore fields are already the classic lib/design/diverge.ts battle's fields (see lib/workflow/summary.ts's summarizeBattle, wired in WQ-016) -- reusing them for Forge's separate battle.ts would conflate two different mechanisms in the one-read-model control surface this session just built, corrupting it rather than extending it. None of these are reasons to deprecate battle.ts (the structural-convergence reuse is sound and the module is well-tested) -- they are concrete missing prerequisites. Follow-up WQ-018 queued with those exact prerequisites as its scope, so the eventual wiring is a real quality upgrade, not a cost/quality regression shipped under a feature name.

tasks.description: Content-safety gate for Forge's generated HTML/CSS/JS (docs/IMPLEMENTATION_GAP.md P2-4, filed during T08/P1-4's file-write-containment proof but never queued). Forge's model output is a whole freeform HTML/CSS/JS document, not data slotted into templates, so the deterministic renderer's field-level guards (safeHref, safeImageUrl, escapeText, escapeAttribute in lib/render/*) don't apply and nothing in lib/forge/ fills the equivalent role. anti-ai-gate.ts checks content for genericity/restraint-contract violations, not for javascript: URLs, inline on*= event-handler attributes, or unauthorized external <script src> domains. Lower priority than the file-write-path concern (the model can't escape the site directory) but a real gap if a vendor's output ever included such a pattern -- accidentally or from a prompt-injection-adjacent path (e.g. scraped web copy quoted back into the HTML-generation prompt in research.ts).
tasks.assignedWorker: claude, deterministic — a content-scan gate following anti-ai-gate.ts's existing flags.push({code,severity,message}) pattern
tasks.inputs: lib/forge/anti-ai-gate.ts, lib/forge/antiPatternSignals.ts, lib/forge/motion.ts (the CDN allowlist), docs/IMPLEMENTATION_GAP.md P2-4
tasks.outputs: checkContentSafety() added to lib/forge/antiPatternSignals.ts: (1) javascript: URLs on href/src/action/formaction (CONTENT_SAFETY_JAVASCRIPT_URL), (2) inline on*= event-handler attributes with a negative-lookbehind guard against hyphenated data-on...= false positives (CONTENT_SAFETY_INLINE_EVENT_HANDLER), (3) <script src> outside a new SCRIPT_SRC_ALLOWLIST (cdn.jsdelivr.net, unpkg.com, cdnjs.cloudflare.com) with exact-or-subdomain matching resistant to substring domain spoofing (CONTENT_SAFETY_UNTRUSTED_SCRIPT_SRC) -- all severity 'fail'. Wired into auditAntiAIGeneric (lib/forge/anti-ai-gate.ts) so it gates delivery like the existing checks. 11 new tests in test/forge/antiPatternSignals.test.ts. Running the full suite against this change surfaced a genuine, previously-undetected real defect: the frozen Ridgeway regression fixture (test/fixtures/forge/ridgeway/site-B-index.html, a real captured Forge run) contains two literal onsubmit="return false;" inline handlers the model actually wrote -- confirmed via a whole-source grep that no live code currently emits onsubmit, so this was genuinely undetected freeform-model output, not a template. test/forge/ridgeway-regression.test.ts's 'full gate passes clean' assertion was narrowed to the axes it was actually testing (structural convergence / forbidden-assumption / restraint / card-grid), and a new test was added asserting the content-safety gate correctly flags this real historical defect -- the frozen fixture itself was left untouched rather than edited or the gate weakened to force a false pass.
